title: Sell Mineral Rights in Opal, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Opal, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Opal, a Lincoln County gas hub on the Moxa Arch and Overthrust Belt? Get an offer priced against actual unit production.
heroLead: Opal is a small town that punches above its weight in the natural gas business, sitting near the Moxa Arch and Overthrust Belt trend that has produced gas in this part of Lincoln County for decades.
intro: Unlike the ranching country further north in Star Valley, the ground around Opal has been developed for natural gas since the mid-twentieth century, with production tied to structural traps along the Moxa Arch and the more complex thrust-belt geology to the west. Interests here are more likely to be active or historically producing than a quiet legacy holding, and we price them against real unit history.

Fontenelle and other fields nearby have added to the production picture in this corner of Lincoln County over the years, and some interests near Opal touch more than one field or unit as boundaries and operators have shifted with new development over the decades.

sections.heading: Moxa Arch and Overthrust Belt geology
paragraphs: This is structurally complicated ground — the Overthrust Belt stacks older rock over younger formations in ways that created some very productive traps but also some very complex title and unit histories. We take extra care tracing your legal description to the correct participating area before pricing.

sections.heading: A long production history
paragraphs: Because gas production near Opal predates a lot of the more recent Green River Basin plays, some interests here have decades of royalty history to draw on, which gives us a solid basis for pricing rather than relying on projections.

sections.heading: What we need
paragraphs: A division order with your decimal interest and unit name is fastest. If you only have an older lease, the legal description lets us trace it through Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission records.

faqs.question: Why is the geology near Opal described as complicated?
faqs.answer: The Overthrust Belt stacks older rock layers over younger ones through geologic faulting, which creates productive traps but also more complex unit and title histories that take extra care to trace.

faqs.question: How long has gas been produced near Opal?
faqs.answer: Decades — this is one of the older gas-producing areas in southwest Wyoming, which means many interests here have long, well-documented production histories.

faqs.question: What if my interest is in an older unit with a confusing name on my check stub?
faqs.answer: Send us what you have. We're used to tracing older Overthrust Belt unit names back to current operators and participating areas.

faqs.question: Is my interest tied to Fontenelle or a different field near Opal?
faqs.answer: It's worth checking specifically — several fields sit close together in this part of Lincoln County, and your division order should name the exact unit.
